subject.title: docs(durable): rebuild 2026.7.1 beta 3 durable core RFC and proof plan

question: Should this release/2026.7.1 split architecture and test plan replace the overlapping main-targeted RFC as the canonical durable-core document, and is its cross-owner boundary approved?
rationale: Both proposals are technically plausible and overlap substantially; selecting the canonical public source, target branch, and permanent core ownership model requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Consolidate on main RFC
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101828 as the canonical proposal and fold in this PR's improved existing-store and proof-plan material.

options.title: Adopt release rebuild
options.body: Publish this split release-specific RFC and test plan, then reconcile or close the earlier main-targeted proposal.

options.title: Pause both proposals
options.body: Defer public architecture publication until the durable-core boundary and implementation sequence receive explicit owner approval.

recommendation.title: Consolidate on main RFC
recommendation.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101828 as the canonical proposal and fold in this PR's improved existing-store and proof-plan material.

likelyOwner.reason: The current database-first contract and SQLite-backed task ownership in the affected area trace most directly to Vincent Koc's recent work.
